edges.description: Loss of Ltbp1 in the mouse produces a lethal conotruncal malformation with reduced TGF-beta activity. Humans with biallelic truncating LTBP1 variants survive, and their cardiac findings are a septal defect, mild valvular insufficiency and mild hypertrophy - none of them conotruncal and none lethal.
edges.limitations: Species difference in LTBP paralog redundancy is the authors' proposed explanation and is not demonstrated. The mouse allele also removes only the long isoform, where the human alleles truncate both, so the comparison is not allele-matched.

nodes.description: The demonstrated human tissue lesion. Electron microscopy of skin from the individual with the c.4844del allele showed microfibrils infiltrating the periphery of the elastic fiber and mild fragmentation of the elastin core, which remained present. The abnormality is mild, matching the mild to moderate clinical cutis laxa rather than the near-absent elastic network seen in some other cutis laxa subtypes.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense or frameshift variants in LTBP1. In the four reported families the alterations fall in the second EGF-like domain (c.1342C>T), the third EGF-like domain (c.4844del), and the 12th and 13th calcium-binding EGF-like domains (c.3991dup and c.4431T>A) of the long isoform. The position matters mechanistically and the two branches below are not interchangeable.

nodes.description: The skeletal arm of the disease. In zebrafish, loss of ltbp1 produces ectopic intramembranous bone on the vertebral neural and haemal arches in both lines, and reduced vertebral tissue mineral density in the line lacking the C-terminal TGF-beta-binding domains. In humans the corresponding features are craniosynostosis, short stature and brachydactyly. The intervening steps are not established, and the direction of any TGF-beta contribution in bone may be opposite to that in skin - see the hypothesis group.

nodes.description: Predates the human disease by fourteen years and was not made to model it. Deleting the long Ltbp1 isoform is perinatally lethal from persistent truncus arteriosus and interrupted aortic arch, with decreased TGF-beta activity in the outflow tract and faulty cardiac neural crest function. Recorded here because the contrast with the human phenotype is informative, not because it recapitulates it.
